title: review: H4 fix round 2: the per-goal reservation cap must not treat the per-run hard cap as a goal budget (it refuses the second parallel dispatch of any role); apply a goal-level cap only where a goal budget exists and estimate from recent runs first (gate_red on T-0392)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain ade6b74, 530c2ab and c1ba47c (T-0362, T-0392) in git log; never drop or amend them.
Gate red on T-0392, reproduced on a clean external run, two failures: tests/test_daemon.py::Daemon::test_depends_on_gates_dispatch (Lists differ: ['T-0001'] != ['T-0001', 'T-0002'], the second ready task is no longer dispatched) and tests/test_pool.py::Reservations::test_goal_role_cap_refuses_when_goal_spend_plus_reservations_exceed_cap (unexpectedly None: the allowed case is refused). Cause: c1ba47c reads role_cap from [limits].max_budget_usd[role], which is the per-run hard cap (execute 6.0 USD), and the estimate for a new reservation is that same cap, so goal_spend + live reservations + est exceeds the "cap" as soon as a second run of the role starts in the same goal; every parallel dispatch of one role is refused.
Fix: (1) separate the two concepts: per-run cap ([limits].max_budget_usd[role]) is only an estimate ceiling, never a goal cap; the goal-level guard applies only when a goal budget for the role is configured ([review].budget_usd for role review, plus an optional new [limits].goal_budget_usd table, default absent = no goal-level cap). Daily account token budgets keep working as before. (2) Estimate order: median tokens and usd of that role's last 20 run rows when at least 5 exist, else the per-run cap. (3) Rewrite test_goal_role_cap_refuses_when_goal_spend_plus_reservations_exceed_cap to use a configured goal budget (over refuses, under allows) and add test_two_parallel_execute_dispatches_allowed_without_goal_budget (two reserve calls for role execute in one goal with only per-run caps configured both succeed). test_depends_on_gates_dispatch must pass unchanged.
Keep the five T-0362 tests and the T-0392 tests green (adjust test_exhausted_hold_releases_dispatch_reservation only if the estimate change requires). Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh from the worktree root until it exits 0 (whole suite), then git add -A and git commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows c1ba47c, 530c2ab and ade6b74 below your commit
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: dispatch() calls pool.pick('execute')/pool.pick_executor(...) to choose account_id purely to gate pool.reserve(), then hands off to spawn_async(_dispatch_worker, t['id'], prompt) — which does NOT receive account_id. The actual run (executor.py:190 pool.pick_executor(...) or spawn.py's own pick) re-selects the account/executor independently. Because pool.reserve() is idempotent keyed only on task id, that second reserve() call silently returns the reservation already made under the FIRST pick, without validating it matches the executor that will actually run the work. If pool state changes between the two picks (cooldowns, other accounts' day_tokens ticking, other reservations), a task can be approved against one account's daily budget headroom and then executed on a different, possibly already-over-budget account — defeating the oversubscription guard this feature exists to add.

_reservation_estimate falls back to est_tokens=0 whenever there are fewer than 5 historical runs for the role AND the account/executor has no usd_per_token/usd-per-token configured (source lookup misses or ratio is falsy). With est_tokens=0, reserve()'s daily-token check `day_used + live_tokens + est_tokens > daily` can never trip for that account no matter how many reservations pile up, silently bypassing the per-account daily budget cap precisely for new/rarely-run accounts or executors — the case the reservation system is most needed for. test_two_parallel_execute_dispatches_allowed_without_goal_budget exercises exactly this gap (no usd_per_token for 'astra', no history) and treats unlimited concurrent reservations as expected.

reserve() runs before stamp(t['id'], 'dispatched_at'). If stamp() fails because another caller already dispatched the same task (e.g. the executor MCP path claims it concurrently), the reservation made here is never released — it sits consuming daily-budget headroom for up to stage_lease_s (default 900s) until sweep_reservations reclaims it, since no process is actually running under this reservation.

reconcile_dead now constructs a brand-new Pool() (full cfg reload, account/executor init, _sync_legacy_codex) once per dead task, inside a loop that can iterate several dead tasks per tick, instead of reusing the pool already passed into tick(). Wasteful and re-triggers legacy-sync side effects repeatedly; not incorrect but avoidable.
